title: Long-Slow Instant Pot Massaman Beef
cookTime: 8–10 hr Low + overnight fridge + 20–30 min reduce
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into 4–5 cm chunks, patted dry
1 jar Massaman curry paste (180–200g; Maesri, Valcom or Ayam)
400ml full-fat coconut milk (not lite, not cream)
1/2 cup beef stock, plus a splash to deglaze if needed
1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar
1 tsp tamarind paste (or lime at the end)
Oil only if the pot looks dry
2–3 waxy potatoes, cut into 3–4 cm chunks (Day 2)
Salt, extra fish sauce and lime, to finish
method: DAY 1 — Sear first. Instant Pot Sauté Normal. A little oil if needed. Sear beef in two batches, 2–3 min a side. Do not crowd. Lift out onto a plate.
If the bottom is dark or sticky, splash of stock and scrape clean.
Onion 2–3 min until soft. Garlic and ginger 1 min.
Whole jar of Massaman paste, 1–2 min until fragrant. Do not use Sauté More — paste burns.
Return beef and juices. Coat in the paste.
Add coconut milk, remaining stock, cinnamon, cardamom, star anise, fish sauce, sugar and tamarind. Scrape the bottom. Liquid should come about two-thirds up the meat.
Cancel Sauté. Slow Cook Low, lid on venting (or glass lid). Cook 8–10 hours. 10 hours is fine. Keep Warm for 1–2 hours after is OK.
Cool 20–30 minutes. Fridge overnight (8–12 hours is enough). Do not reduce yet. Do not add potatoes or peanuts yet.
DAY 2 — Scoop off the solid white fat. Bin most of it.

Instant Pot Sauté Normal, lid off. Reduce 15–25 minutes, stirring, until it is a thick gravy that coats a spoon. Stay saucy — do not take it rendang-dry. Drop to Less if it starts catching. Splash of coconut milk if it goes too tight.
Add potatoes. Simmer 15–20 minutes until just tender.
Stir in peanuts for the last 5 minutes.
Taste: fish sauce for salt, sugar if sharp, lime if heavy. Rest 10 minutes. Serve with jasmine rice and cucumber.
timing: Day 1: sear and build sauce ~20 min, Slow Cook Low 8–10 hours lid on venting, optional Keep Warm 1–2 hours, cool, fridge overnight. Day 2: skim fat, Sauté reduce 15–25 min to thick gravy, potatoes 15–20 min, peanuts 5 min, rest 10 min.
summary: Jar-paste Massaman the same way as the long-slow rendang: sear first, coconut milk, 8–10 hr Low, overnight fridge, then a saucy Sauté reduce. Potatoes and peanuts go in on day 2.
notes: No pressure cook. Long Slow Cook Low plus fridge rest is the point.
Use full-fat coconut milk, not cream and not lite.
Massaman should stay a thick gravy, not dry and clinging like rendang.
Do not add potatoes or peanuts on day 1 or they turn to mush.
